items.item: exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 (advisory, order-influencing exit head on trend_donchian / trend_donchian_sol / trend_donchian_eth) — investigate silence + demote

part_a_why_silent.measured_silence: last_seen 2026-09-22T17:06:08.456783+00:00 (MEASURED, api/bot/shadow/stats, read 2026-09-24T22:24Z — issue #12906) — ~53h with zero predictions at the time of this read.
part_a_why_silent.why_no_registry_entry: MEASURED (trainer-vm-diag #12907/#12910): this artifact is NOT produced by the standard `python -m ml train` / ml.registry-store pathway at all. `scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py` (module docstring, read this session) is a standalone, manually-invoked Tier-1 tool that writes a flat, self-contained JSON artifact directly to `runtime_logs/trainer_mirror/exit_head/<model_id>.json` — model_id, family, tf, stage, features, shape, booster_txt, trained_at, train window — with NO ml.registry-store row, NO StageEvent history, and NO call site in `run_training_cycle.sh`'s manifest loop (grep of run_training_cycle.sh / publish_trainer_mirror.sh confirms export_exit_head.py is referenced only in comments, never invoked). `promote-stage`/`gate-check` operate on `ml/registry-store/*.json` (ModelRegistry.get() raises 'no registry entry for <id>' when absent — exactly PI-20260924-JQHBBTOS-0001's observed failure), which is a DIFFERENT store this artifact was never written into. This is not a data-loss bug; it is a second, parallel, hand-run promotion mechanism for exit-head artifacts that the standard registry tooling cannot see.
part_a_why_silent.why_silent_since_2026-09-22T17:06Z: PARTIALLY diagnosed, not fully. `exit_head_model: exit-head-donchian-1h-v1` is declared (config/strategies.yaml, read this session) on exactly THREE legs: `trend_donchian` (BTCUSDT), `trend_donchian_sol` (SOLUSDT), `trend_donchian_eth` (ETHUSDT) — the scorer only fires from `trend_donchian.monitor()` when one of these three has an OPEN position, per src/runtime/exit_head_shadow.py's own docstring ('closed native bar per open donchian-family trade'). MEASURED (api/bot/trades/closed?limit=200, issue #12909, and api/bot/positions?include_paper=true, issue #12908, both read 2026-09-24T22:2x Z): none of the three legs is in the CURRENT open-positions list; in the last 200 closed trades, `trend_donchian` (BTC) last closed 2026-09-21T08:48:37Z, `trend_donchian_sol` last closed 2026-09-21T14:04:32Z — both BEFORE the silence began — and `trend_donchian_eth` last closed 2026-09-22T18:32:21Z, i.e. it was STILL OPEN through and past the 17:06:08Z last-prediction timestamp, closing ~86 minutes later. So the bulk of the ~53h silence is substantially explained by these three specific legs having had almost no open-position time since 2026-09-22T17:06Z (two were already flat before the silence started, the third stayed open only ~86 more minutes) — NOT a crash: journalctl for ict-trader-live across 2026-09-22T16:40-17:25Z (issue #12906) and 17:00-17:12Z (issue #12908) shows the service running continuously, ticking every strategy including the donchian legs, with no traceback/exception near 17:06. NOT established this session: whether the ~86-minute eth-still-open window (17:06→18:32) should have produced at least one more scoring event and didn't (a genuine single-firing gap), versus the observed ~84min cadence_seconds_est simply not landing another 1h-bar-close inside that window by chance. This narrower question is unresolved and is filed to the pipeline rather than guessed at.
part_a_why_silent.correction_to_PI-20260924-JQHBBTOS-0001: That row's 'roughly 37 missed firings' framing (derived from dividing the ~53h gap by the historical average cadence_seconds_est~84min) reads as an ongoing pipeline failure. MEASURED this session: it is closer to 'almost nothing to score' — two of the three wired legs were already flat before the gap began and the third was open for only the first ~86 minutes of it. The registry-gap finding (part of PI-0001) stands unchanged; the '~37 missed firings' characterization is likely an overstatement of how many scoring opportunities actually existed, and is corrected here rather than re-asserted.

part_b_demote.operator_authorization: 'Investigate + demote (Recommended)', operator popup in manager session session_01Ljhs6sFAdWHdMDhJpL5aBP, ~21:50Z 2026-09-24, relayed via this lane's task notification — the required Tier-3 approval for an advisory-→shadow flip (per drift-remediation skill step 5: demote is fail-permissive/interim, still Tier-3, but does not itself require a further round-trip once approved).
part_b_demote.mechanism_found: There is no git-tracked file to change and no `promote-stage` equivalent for this artifact (see part_a). The artifact's `stage` field is a flat key in the exported JSON itself (`runtime_logs/trainer_mirror/exit_head/exit-head-donchian-1h-v1.json` on the trainer VM, gitignored runtime data — confirmed not tracked in git: `git ls-files` finds nothing under runtime_logs/). The 'repo's normal mechanism' for THIS artifact type is re-running `scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py --stage shadow ...` (as was originally done with `--stage advisory` to reach today's live state, per the script's own docstring calling that step 'E3 graduation, Tier-3'). Re-running the full export requires reconstructing the original --family-dir/training args and risks producing a materially different booster from a fresh fit. The minimal, correct, `promote_stage()`-equivalent action is a surgical in-place field flip of `stage` only (booster_txt/features/shape/family/tf untouched) — exactly what the standard registry's own promote_stage() does for a registered model (append a stage transition, never retrain).
part_b_demote.action_taken: DONE. MEASURED, trainer-vm-diag #12911, run 36068023081, 2026-09-24T22:32:5x Z: read the artifact's non-booster fields first (model_id=exit-head-donchian-1h-v1, family=donchian, tf=1h, stage=advisory (before), symbols=[BTCUSDT,ETHUSDT,SOLUSDT], trained_at=2026-07-12T14:44:43Z, train_rows=34338, train_trades=1662 — confirms the artifact has not been re-exported/retrained since 2026-07-12, consistent with the mirror dir listing's mtime `Jul 12 14:44` on exit-head-donchian-1h-v1.json, issue #12910). Patched ONLY the `stage` key in place (booster_txt/features/shape/family/tf/symbols untouched, asserted before-value == 'advisory' before writing) — verified read-back on the trainer side: `stage now: shadow`. Republished via `bash scripts/ops/publish_trainer_mirror.sh` (the same channel the automated daily cycle uses, not a bespoke path): output ends `{"ts":"2026-09-24T22:32:55+00:00","status":"published","dest":"ubuntu@141.145.193.91:/data/bot-data/runtime_logs/trainer_mirror"}` — the rsync to the live VM's mirror path completed successfully.
part_b_demote.any_write_refused: No. The patch (a local file write on the trainer VM, via the already-autonomous trainer-vm-diag relay) and the publish (the standard, pre-existing publish_trainer_mirror.sh channel) both succeeded without any permission refusal.
part_b_demote.not_yet_verified: The live VM's SERVED behavior (a shadow_predictions.jsonl row with model_id=exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 and stage='shadow') has not been observed yet, because none of the three wired legs (trend_donchian / trend_donchian_sol / trend_donchian_eth) currently has an open position to score (see part_a) — there is nothing for the scorer to fire on right now. This is a genuine soak-style wait, not a gap in the mechanism: the file-level change is confirmed on both the trainer canonical copy and (via the publish log) the live mirror destination. Filed to the pipeline with an observation due_when so a later session confirms the first post-patch prediction actually logs stage=shadow once any of the three legs next opens a donchian trade.
